main_body: Open three-tier wooden shelf unit with a dark recessed back, scrolls and books on the shelves, and a dark plinth at the bottom
top_band: Light tan band at rows 1-4, with a darker orange edge row at about row 4 and a dark interior starting at row 5
evidence: Reading one column down the middle: a light tan top band (rows 1-4), a darker edge row, then the dark shadowed shelf interiors (rows 5-10). Below that come 1-2 row shelf boards and more recessed bays down to the plinth. The top is thin, but a foreshortened surface of about 4 rows with a front edge line and an inset, shadowed interior is enough to read as a cabinet top with an eave. The shelf boards themselves are thin front edges, so this is borderline.

style.evidence: The outline is a dark brown/maroon tinted to the neighbouring wood, so it does not look like a sticker. The wood uses only about 4 steps (light tan, orange, mid brown, dark brown), against 5-6 in the reference. The top band and the maroon shelf backs are large flat fills of 5x5 pixels or more with no grain or speckle. Only the small items (scrolls, books, jars) carry any detail. Tile density is below the reference, which has richer grain and per-element shading.
